Resolves #18889

`Neo.worker.App#importApp()` filters its lazy webpack context with `webpackInclude`. The pattern needed a path segment after `docs/app`, so the docs app's entry, `docs/app.mjs`, never entered the context. A bundled App worker had no chunk for it, and `dist/production/docs` threw `Cannot find module './docs/app.mjs'`. The include now adds the docs entry and keeps every path it matched before:

```
/(?:apps|docs\/app|examples|src)\/.*app\.mjs$/          before
/(?:(?:apps|docs\/app|examples|src)\/.*|docs\/)app\.mjs$/   after
```

Evidence: L3 (a production App-worker build from this branch, loaded in Chromium) → L3 required (AC-2 is a production load). Residual: none.

Micro-review eligible: contained — one magic comment and the arm that pins it.

## AC Evidence

| AC | |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `unit/worker/ImportAppInclude.spec.mjs` reads the include from `src/worker/App.mjs` and tests it on absolute paths, as webpack does. The docs, portal, examples and `src` entries match; a root `app.mjs` does not. Red on `dev`: only the docs arm fails |
| AC-2 | outside CI, below: the production App worker from this branch holds the entry, and `dist/production/docs/index.html` boots |

## Deltas from ticket

- None. The fix is the ticket's pattern, and both ACs are met as written.

## Test Evidence

Production App worker (`buildThreads -f -n -t app -e prod`), read back and loaded:

| Include | `"./docs/app.mjs"` in `appworker.js`'s context map | `dist/production/docs/index.html` |
|---|---|---|
| `dev` | 0 (the portal entry: 1) | `pageerror Cannot find module './docs/app.mjs'`; 0 viewports, 0 components |
| this branch | 1 | boots: 1 viewport, 1272 components, no console error |

The arm's root is synthetic (`/opt/neo`). A checkout whose own path runs through `apps/`, `examples/` or `src/` matches every entry below it, whatever the include says about the entries. That ancestor case is the ticket's Out of Scope.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The premise is that the include needed a segment after `docs/app`, so the docs entry itself never entered the context. I checked the old and new patterns against every tracked path (`git ls-files`, prefixed with a synthetic root). The new include adds exactly `docs/app.mjs` and drops nothing the old one matched. At `e85333b242`, `unit/worker/ImportAppInclude.spec.mjs` passes 5/5. Against `dev`'s `src/worker/App.mjs`, exactly the docs arm fails, as the PR says. Reading the comment out of the source and testing absolute paths is the right instrument for a build-time directive. One observation, not a finding: the `docs\/` alternative is as unanchored as its siblings, so a `mydocs/app.mjs` would match; no tracked file does. I did not rebuild the production App worker (AC-2), and the verdict does not rest on it.
